Each plan drew 5 findings and every one was folded after being verified against the real artefacts. Either defect alone would have shipped a launch requirement whose proof proves nothing, which is precisely the failure mode the charter's opt-out gate exists to prevent. A MEDIUM CAUGHT THE ACCOUNT I DENIED THIS SESSION: the e03 writer consulted verdicts for display but never for WRITES, so GCGH159 passed the plan's own publishable() predicate and would have been written into the corpus despite carrying a denied verdict. The fix adds a denied-verdict clause to publishable() and a test feeding GCGH159 through it. Another medium found F052's opt-out promise copy OVERCLAIMS: after a total devs opt-out the person is still named across briefing, stats, graph and signal pages, so the promise to 'remove what is live within one deploy cycle' was false as written; it is being scoped to the developer profile and index entry with the public-signal citations named explicitly. I reproduced it before acting and WITHDREW the clearing in d78ab37 rather than denying him: there is no evidence of automation and inventing one repeats the error in the opposite direction. The flag now stands unresolved and he publishes nowhere.
